subject: business-studies
title: Generic Strategies in Action
welcome_lead: Cost leadership, differentiation, focus - and when each wins.
meta_desc: A-Level Strategy: Porter's generic strategies with examples.
final_note: Pick one strategy, commit fully, and align every function behind it.

concepts.def: Lowest unit cost in the industry.
Unique offering commanding a price premium.
Lowest cost in a narrow niche.
Unique premium offer to a niche.
Attempt to combine low cost and differentiation.
Activities through which a firm creates value.

walkthroughs.body_html: Cost leadership requires scale, tight cost control, experience curves and lean operations. It often means commodity-style products with little frill - and slim per-unit profit but massive volume.
Differentiation requires brand investment, innovation and customer experience. The premium covers higher costs and produces fatter margins - Apple is the canonical case.
Focus strategies concentrate on a tightly defined segment. Specialist tailors, niche hot sauces and Morgan Cars all show focus working at small scale where broad players cannot serve well.

mcqs.q: What are Porter's two main generic strategies for competitive advantage?
options: Cost leadership (being the lowest-cost producer) and differentiation (offering unique value customers will pay more for) — Porter argues firms should choose one or the other.
Porter says businesses should pursue both low cost and differentiation at once.
